name: El Puerto (Harbour & Old Centre)
tagline: Cudillero's postcard heart, stacked houses and fishing boats
description: The harbour and old centre is the Cudillero everyone pictures: brightly painted houses climbing a cliff amphitheatre above a working fishing port. It's the liveliest area, packed with marisquerias, sidrerias and small shops, but also the steepest and most crowded, especially midday in summer when day-trippers fill the plaza and quay.
bestFor: Short stays, seafood lovers, first-time visitors who want to be in the thick of it
pros: Iconic views and photo spots everywhere
Best concentration of restaurants and bars
cons: Crowded and noisy in peak summer

name: El Pito
tagline: The quieter upper village above the cliffs
description: El Pito sits on flatter ground above Cudillero's harbour, home to the town hall, a school, and more everyday local life away from the tourist crush below. It's less scenic than the harbour but far more practical for longer stays, with easier parking, quieter streets, and a short walk or drive down into the old centre.
bestFor: Longer stays, remote workers wanting quiet, anyone with a car
pros: Easier parking than the harbour area
Good base for exploring the wider coast

name: Playa del Silencio (near Novellana)
tagline: A dramatic, cliff-framed beach a short drive west
description: Playa del Silencio, near the village of Novellana about 15 to 20 minutes from Cudillero by car, is one of Asturias's most striking beaches: a cove framed by cliffs, rock formations, and a small waterfall. It's a nature and photography destination rather than a place to stay, with very limited services and no real accommodation cluster of its own.
bestFor: Day trips, hiking, photography, beach lovers with a car
pros: Far quieter than the harbour in early morning
Great hiking and coastal path access
cons: Requires a car or long walk to reach

name: Luarca
tagline: A larger coastal town about 30 minutes west
description: Luarca, roughly a 30-minute drive west along the coast, is a bigger fishing town with its own harbour, more restaurants and shops, a hospital, and noticeably more year-round infrastructure than Cudillero. It's a practical alternative base for longer stays or anyone who wants Cudillero's coastal charm with more day-to-day services on hand.
vibe: Bigger, more functional, still coastal and scenic
bestFor: Longer stays needing more services, day trips, a base with more restaurant variety
pros: More shops, services and restaurant variety
Better bus connections along the coast
cons: Less intimate and dramatic than Cudillero's cliffside setting
